options: Change the costume to the jumping costume
Change the backdrop to the menu
mcqs.why: In the trampoline task the costume is changed to the 'jumping' costume when the sprite goes up, and switched back to the normal costume when it lands on the trampoline.

mcqs.q: An advantage of writing a function instead of repeating the same instructions everywhere is:
options: A mistake can be corrected in one place only
The code is duplicated many times
The script becomes harder to read
mcqs.why: A function groups instructions under one name: the code is shorter and tidier, nothing is repeated, and a mistake can be corrected in one place only.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a limit of Scratch?
options: It has no sounds or costumes
It is slower and less powerful for very large or complex programs
It works only without a stage
mcqs.why: Scratch is designed for learning: it is slower and less powerful than text-based languages for very large programs, and files, databases and detailed 3D graphics are limited.

mcqs.q: Scripts in Scratch are usually started by the Events block:
mcqs.why: The Events category starts scripts when something happens — 'when green flag clicked' is the most common starting block of a Scratch script.

lessons.title: The Internet, Digital Footprints and Online Ethics
lessons.notes_html:
What Is the Internet?

The Internet is a worldwide network of networks that connects millions of computers, mobiles and other devices. Through it, people can share information, communicate by email and messages, study (e-Learning), shop, bank and use social media from anywhere in the world. Studying from home through the Internet is called e-Learning.

Digital Footprints

A digital footprint, also known as a Digital Dossier, is the trail of traces a person leaves while using the internet — posts, comments, likes, searches, photos, location and purchase history. It is the impression of a user that he leaves while using the Internet. Footprints can be active (things we post ourselves) or passive (data collected about us). We should manage them carefully because they build our online impression and reputation.

Ethics and the Ethical Use of the Digital Environment

Ethics are the moral rules that tell us what is right and wrong in our behaviour. Ethical use of the digital environment means: respect others online and never bully or troll; do not copy or use content written by others without permission; do not hack, spam or spread false information; protect your own and others' privacy; share business ideas and personal data carefully (do not share your business ideas with others carelessly); and follow the laws and rules of the platforms you use. A good digital citizen keeps privacy settings on, never uploads inappropriate content, and avoids friend requests from strangers.

Intellectual Property Rights

Intellectual property (IP) means creations of the mind — books, music, inventions, software, designs, brand names and artwork. Intellectual property rights are the legal rights that protect these creations, so that only the owner can use, sell or copy them for a certain time, and others must take permission. Main types: (1) Copyright for books, songs, films, pictures and software. (2) Patent for new inventions. (3) Trademark for brand names and logos. (4) Trade secrets for confidential business information. These rights encourage creativity and invention, and using someone's work without permission is a violation.

Disadvantages of the Internet

Three disadvantages of the Internet are: (1) Cyber crimes such as hacking, fraud and identity theft. (2) Harmful or inappropriate content and cyberbullying, especially for children. (3) Addiction and waste of time on social media and games, which affects health and studies; viruses and spam are further problems.

Key Points

  • The Internet is called the network of networks.
  • A digital footprint is also known as a Digital Dossier.
  • Copyright and trademark are examples of intellectual property rights.

mcqs.q: The Internet is also called the network of:
mcqs.why: The Internet is called the network of networks because it joins millions of separate networks all over the world into one worldwide network.

mcqs.q: Studying from home through the Internet is called:
mcqs.why: Studying from home through the Internet is called e-Learning — learning through electronic means such as online classes and recorded lectures.

mcqs.q: A digital footprint is also known as:
mcqs.why: A digital footprint is also known as a Digital Dossier — the complete trail of traces a person leaves while using the internet.

mcqs.q: A digital footprint is:
options: The impression and traces a user leaves while using the Internet
A shoe print stored in a computer
A password saved in the browser
mcqs.why: A digital footprint is the impression of a user that he leaves while using the Internet — his posts, comments, searches, photos and other traces.

mcqs.q: To stay safe online, we should keep our privacy settings:
mcqs.why: The advice 'keep your privacy settings always off' is wrong: privacy settings should always be kept on so that personal information is shared only with known people.

mcqs.q: Uploading inappropriate content online is:
options: Wrong — it must never be done
A good way to become famous
mcqs.why: A good digital citizen never uploads inappropriate content online; such content harms others, damages the uploader's digital footprint and can be a cyber crime.

mcqs.q: Using the content written by others without their permission is:
options: Allowed if we change one word
A right of every internet user
mcqs.why: We should not use the content written by others without their permission; it is protected by intellectual property rights such as copyright.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an example of an intellectual property right?
options: Copyright over a book or song
mcqs.why: Copyright — the right of an author, artist or programmer over his book, song, picture or software — is an intellectual property right; trademark over a brand name or logo is another example.

mcqs.q: A trademark protects:
mcqs.why: A trademark is the right over a brand name or logo, so no other business can use the same name or mark; a patent, by contrast, protects a new invention.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of the Internet?
options: Cyber crimes such as hacking and identity theft
mcqs.why: Disadvantages of the Internet include cyber crimes (hacking, fraud, identity theft), harmful content and cyberbullying, and addiction and waste of time — while fast communication and e-Learning are advantages.

lessons.title: Cyber Crimes: Hacking, Spam and Social Engineering
lessons.notes_html:
Cyber Crimes and Hacking

Crimes that are committed through the internet are called cyber crimes. Hacking is breaking into someone else's computer system or account without permission. Hackers break into other people's computer systems to steal important data and to destroy the system. Hacking is a cyber crime and is punishable by law.

Spamming and How to Avoid It

Spamming refers to sending an email from an unidentified source — bulk, unwanted messages sent to many people. Measures to avoid spam: preview your message before opening it, and do not click on spam email or its links and attachments. Spam emails often have an unidentified or slightly misspelled sender address, a general greeting like 'Dear Customer', urgent threats or unbelievable prizes, spelling mistakes, and requests for passwords or bank details — genuine companies never ask for these by email.

Email Spoofing

In email spoofing, the criminal changes the 'From' address of an email so it appears to come from a trusted person or company, such as a bank. The victim trusts the fake email and may click a harmful link or share passwords and bank details. Checking the real sender address and not clicking unknown links protects against it.

Social Engineering

Social engineering is the technique used by cybercriminals to attain information from individuals — tricking people into giving their passwords, OTPs or bank details themselves, instead of breaking into the computer technically.

Cyberbullying: Stop and Prevent

Two ways to stop cyberbullying: (1) Do not respond to the bully; block and report the account on the platform, and save the messages as evidence. (2) Inform a trusted adult — parents or teacher — and, in serious cases, report to the FIA Cybercrime Wing. Ways to prevent it: keep privacy settings on and share personal information only with known people; avoid friend requests from strangers; never upload inappropriate content; treat others online with the same respect as face to face; and tell parents or teachers immediately if it happens.

Key Points

  • Crimes committed through the internet are called cyber crimes.
  • Preview messages before opening them and never click spam email.
  • Social engineering tricks people into giving information themselves.

mcqs.q: Why do hackers break into other people's computer systems?
options: To repair the system free of cost
To steal important data and to destroy the system
mcqs.why: Hackers break into other people's computer systems to steal important data and to destroy or damage the system — hacking is a cyber crime punishable by law.

mcqs.q: Crimes that are committed through the internet are called:
mcqs.why: Crimes committed through the internet — such as hacking, fraud, identity theft and cyberbullying — are called cyber crimes.

mcqs.q: According to the book, spamming refers to:
options: Sending an email from an unidentified source
Sending an email to a friend
mcqs.why: The book defines spamming as sending an email from an unidentified source — unwanted bulk messages that should not be opened or clicked.

mcqs.q: Which measures help us avoid spam?
options: Click all links in unknown emails
Reply to spam with your details
Preview the message before opening it and never click on spam email
mcqs.why: To avoid spam: preview your message before opening it, and do not click on spam email, its links or its attachments — delete it and mark it as spam.

mcqs.q: The technique used by cybercriminals to attain information from individuals is called:
mcqs.why: Social engineering is the technique by which cybercriminals trick individuals into giving information — such as passwords and OTPs — themselves.

mcqs.q: To protect your computer, you should install:
options: Unknown free software from any site
mcqs.why: The advice 'don't install updated antivirus' is wrong: an updated antivirus must be installed and the operating system kept updated to protect the computer from viruses and hacking.

mcqs.q: Friend requests from strangers should be:
mcqs.why: We should avoid friend requests from strangers, because criminals use fake profiles to collect personal information and commit fraud.

mcqs.q: In email spoofing, the criminal:
options: Changes the 'From' address so the email looks like it comes from a trusted person or company
Writes the email in another language
mcqs.why: In email spoofing the 'From' address is faked to look like a bank or trusted person, so the victim trusts the email and may share passwords or bank details.

mcqs.q: If a student is being cyberbullied, the first steps are to:
options: Delete all evidence and stay silent
Share the bully's messages with everyone
Not respond, block and report the bully, and inform parents or a teacher
mcqs.why: To stop cyberbullying: do not respond to the bully; block and report the account and save the messages as evidence; and inform a trusted adult or the FIA Cybercrime Wing in serious cases.

mcqs.q: An email that says 'Dear Customer, you have won a prize! Click this link and enter your bank PIN' is most likely:
mcqs.why: Unbelievable prizes, a general greeting, urgency and a request for a bank PIN are classic signs of spam and phishing; genuine companies never ask for PINs or passwords by email.

lessons.title: Online Transaction Fraud, Social Media and Staying Safe Online
lessons.notes_html:
Types of Online Transaction Fraud

  • Identity theft: using someone's personal data (CNIC, card number, passwords) to make transactions in the victim's name.
  • Banking fraud: fake calls, emails or websites obtain bank details and empty the account.
  • Job fraud: fake job advertisements demand registration fees or personal data and disappear.
  • Shopping fraud: fake online stores take advance payment and never send the goods.
  • Phishing: fake emails/sites that steal login details.

A cyber troll — a person who posts upsetting messages online — is not a transaction fraud.

How to Avoid Hacking and Email Hacking

We can avoid hacking by: using strong passwords and changing them regularly; keeping the operating system and apps updated; installing updated antivirus software; not plugging in devices we are not sure about; not opening spam emails or unknown links; keeping privacy settings on; and avoiding friend requests and messages from strangers. These same measures — changing passwords, updating the operating system and not plugging in unknown devices — protect email accounts from hacking.

Protecting Computers

Common protections: install and update antivirus software; keep the operating system and programs updated; use strong passwords and change them regularly; turn on the firewall; back up important data; download only from trusted sources; and avoid spam links and unknown USB devices. If computers are not protected, viruses and malware can delete or steal data, hackers can break in and misuse accounts, the system can slow down or crash, and the user can suffer money loss and privacy loss.

Social Media: Advantages and Disadvantages

Social media means websites and apps (such as Facebook, WhatsApp, YouTube and Instagram) that let people create and share content and connect with others online. Advantages: easy connection with distant friends and relatives; learning about culture and the world; business promotion, selling goods and services and advertising income; entertainment and quick sharing of news. Disadvantages: addiction and waste of time; health effects of excessive use; cyberbullying and cyberstalking; sale or misuse of personal data and identity fraud; and spread of false information. Used with care and time limits, social media is a benefit; used carelessly, it is harmful.

Key Points

  • Identity theft, banking fraud and job fraud are transaction frauds; a cyber troll is not.
  • Change passwords regularly and keep the operating system updated.
  • Social media is useful with care and harmful when used carelessly.

mcqs.q: Which of the following measures helps to avoid email hacking?
options: Use the same password for every account forever
mcqs.why: Avoiding email hacking requires changing passwords regularly, keeping the operating system updated, and not plugging in devices you are not sure about — sharing passwords or never updating does the opposite.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a transaction fraud?
mcqs.why: Identity theft, banking fraud and job fraud all cheat people during online transactions; a cyber troll only posts upsetting messages and is not a transaction fraud.

mcqs.q: Using someone's personal data to make transactions in his name is called:
mcqs.why: Identity theft means the criminal steals personal data (CNIC, card number, passwords) and makes transactions in the victim's name.

mcqs.q: In job fraud, the criminals usually:
options: Publish fake job offers and demand fees or personal data
mcqs.why: Job fraud works through fake job advertisements that demand registration fees or personal data and then disappear.

mcqs.q: Fake emails or websites that steal login details are called:
mcqs.why: Phishing uses fake emails and websites that look genuine to steal login details such as usernames and passwords.

mcqs.q: If a computer is not protected, one possible result is:
options: Viruses and malware can delete or steal data
mcqs.why: Without protection — antivirus, updates, strong passwords, firewall and backups — viruses and malware can delete or steal data, hackers can misuse accounts, and the user can suffer money and privacy loss.

lessons.title: Entrepreneurship and the Business Plan
lessons.notes_html:
Entrepreneurship in the Digital Age

Entrepreneurship refers to the convenience of launching a business online. Entrepreneurship in the digital age means starting and running a business online — launching products or services through the internet and promoting them with digital marketing. A digital entrepreneur uses websites, social media, email and search engines to reach customers at low cost, receives orders and payments online, and grows the business from anywhere.

The Business Plan

A business plan is a document setting out the objectives of the business. Its key components are: executive summary (the whole plan summarised), business description, market research, products/services, marketing plan, operations, team, and financial plan/forecast. Benefits: it gives clear objectives and strategies, helps get loans or investors, foresees costs and risks, and measures progress. Without a business plan, a business works without direction — money is wasted, mistakes repeat, and the chance of failure increases greatly.

Executive Summary and Value Proposition

The entire business plan is summarised in the executive summary, which is read first by investors and partners. A value proposition is a simple statement that summarises why a customer would choose your product or service.

Market Research

The marketing process also involves identifying a potential market, assessing the size of the market, and determining an approximate estimate of the product's value. Good market research tells the entrepreneur who the customers are and what they are willing to pay.

Creativity and Obstacles

A digital entrepreneur can enhance creativity by: studying customers and competitors for new ideas; following trends and new technologies; brainstorming with a team; experimenting with new content formats such as videos, reels and stories; taking feedback from customers and improving products; and learning new digital tools and skills regularly. Obstacles faced by digital entrepreneurship include: strong online competition; shortage of money and skilled staff at the start; fast-changing technology and platform rules; online fraud, hacking and payment risks; building customer trust without a physical shop; poor internet access in some areas; and difficulty in reaching the right audience among millions of online users.

Key Points

  • Entrepreneurship means launching a business — in the digital age, online.
  • The executive summary summarises the entire business plan.
  • A value proposition states why a customer would choose your product.

lessons.title: Digital Marketing and Its Components
lessons.notes_html:
Digital Marketing

Digital marketing, also called online marketing, is the promotion of brands to connect with potential customers using the internet and other forms of digital communication. It is not called 'inline marketing'. The goals of digital marketing are: to promote brands and connect with potential customers; to increase sales and business growth; to reach a large, targeted audience at low cost; to build a good online reputation through positive reviews; to increase website traffic (including through SEO and paid search); and to keep customers informed and loyal through messages, emails and social media. Advertisement is a component of digital marketing.

Components of a Digital Marketing Plan

Components include: business goals and objectives; target audience/market research; value proposition; website and SEO; content marketing; social media marketing; email marketing; online advertising (paid search and display ads); mobile and video marketing; budget; and measuring results (analytics) with quality assurance. Four components explained: (1) Executive summary and goals. (2) Market research and value proposition. (3) Channels and content — SEO, social media, email, video and paid advertising. (4) Budget, quality assurance and measurement.

Types of Digital Marketing

  • Content marketing: creating and sharing useful, interesting content — articles, blogs, pictures and videos — to attract and engage a target audience instead of directly advertising a product.
  • Email marketing: a direct marketing scheme that involves sending promotional messages to customers by email — new products, offers, discounts and newsletters. Email is definitely used for marketing.
  • Video marketing: enables companies to connect with customers in a more visually engaging and cooperating way.
  • Reputation marketing: focuses on gathering and endorsing positive online reviews.
  • Paid search: increases the visibility of a website in search engines; hashtags help people to find your tweets on social media.

SEO and Optimising a Website

SEO (Search Engine Optimisation) focuses on improving the natural (unpaid) traffic to a website by making it rank higher in search engine results, so customers searching for related words find our website first. The four steps to optimising a website are: (1) Research — find the keywords customers search for and study competitors. (2) On-page optimisation — use keywords in titles, headings and content, and improve page quality and loading speed. (3) Technical optimisation — make the site mobile-friendly, secure (HTTPS) and easy for search engines to crawl and index. (4) Off-page optimisation and review — build quality links and reputation, then measure traffic and keep improving.

Social Media Marketing

Social media marketing is promoting products and brands through social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram and YouTube. It helps a start-up because it is free or cheap, reaches many customers quickly, builds a brand image, and lets the owner talk directly with customers. When selecting a platform, consider: where your target customers are (young customers on TikTok/Instagram, professionals on LinkedIn); the type of product (clothes and food sell well with photos and short videos); cost and features; and your content ability.

Key Points

  • Digital marketing is also called online marketing.
  • Email marketing sends promotional messages to customers.
  • SEO improves the natural (unpaid) traffic of a website.

lessons.title: Transactions, Payments and Using Digital Platforms for Business
lessons.notes_html:
Transaction and Payment

A transaction is an instance of buying or selling something; the act of agreement between a buyer and a seller is referred to as a transaction. A transaction is the complete act of buying or selling — it includes choosing the product, agreeing the price, paying and receiving the goods. Payment is only one part of it: the actual transfer of money from buyer to seller.

Making Safe Payments

Safe payments: pay only on trusted, secure websites (https); use known methods such as bank transfer, cards or cash on delivery; never share OTP, PIN or passwords with anyone; avoid public Wi-Fi for banking; check statements regularly; and keep receipts/screenshots of every payment.

Quality Assurance

The way to prevent mistakes is called quality assurance. In a digital marketing plan, quality assurance checks content, links, prices and offers before and after publishing, so that customers receive correct information and the business keeps its good reputation.

Using Digital Marketing Platforms to Enhance a Business

A business can be enhanced by: creating a business website and optimising it with SEO so customers find it on Google; opening business pages on Facebook and Instagram and posting regular photos, videos and offers, using hashtags so people can find the posts; using WhatsApp Business for direct orders and customer support; running small paid-search and social-media ad campaigns targeted at the city and age group; collecting and displaying positive customer reviews (reputation marketing); sending promotional emails to regular customers; and checking the results monthly to spend more on the platform that brings the most sales.

Key Points

  • A transaction is the complete act of buying or selling; payment is only the transfer of money.
  • Never share OTP, PIN or passwords with anyone.
  • Quality assurance is the way to prevent mistakes.
